advances: An explicit mixed source with two integer and two continuous dimensions. Its small fibers converge weakly to a centroid atom, and the response uses the surviving normal motion at scale square root of t. Its normalized depth is above 1/9 for small positive t.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The shear has determinant one and the two powers of $t$ in the diagonal map add to one, so $|E_t|=tV$. Also $E_t$ shrinks to the interior point $g$, so $E_t\subset\operatorname{int}T$ for small $t>0$. Apply e1209ac9a9de7caa with $a=V$. It verifies the exact seven-fiber support and mass, and gives the six-fiber through-mark formula
$$
A_{6,t}(y)=\min_{\|u\|=1}[F_T(y,u)+tP_t(u,y)].
$$
Here $F_T$ is the $T$ cap area and $P_t$ is the minimum over opposite shifts about $u\cdot y$ of the two upper $E_t$ cap areas divided by $t$. The formula is unchanged by positive rescaling of the normal and the shift. The same fact gives the seven-fiber local depth $tV+A_{6,t}(y)$ near $g$, attained maximizing sets with $y=g+O(t)$ there, and all other base bounds.

At a mark $g+tv_t$, the canonical trial normals give $\Gamma V+O(t)$ since the shifted pair can saturate with cost $P_t\le V$. By 53fe12b742a7608d the $T$ cap at $g$ has area at least $\Gamma V$, with equality only for the three canonical rays. Any sequence of minimizing normals, or of normals with cap cost within $o(t)$ of that minimum, therefore approaches the union of these rays, by continuity, compactness and nonnegativity of the added cost. We evaluate each subsequential case.

Near the $l_1$ ray use $u=(1,\delta)$ with $\delta\to0$. Only $e_1$ is strictly on the included side for all sufficiently small $t$. Multiplying the edge fractions gives
$$
F_T(g+tv_t,u)=\frac{V}{1-\delta}
 \left[\frac{2-\delta}{3}-t(v_{t,1}+\delta v_{t,2})\right]^2.
$$
In particular $F_T(g,u)=\Gamma V+V\delta^2/[9(1-\delta)]$ and the change from moving $g$ to $g+tv_t$ is $-t\kappa v_1+o(t)$ for $\delta\to0$. Thus any competing sequence of total cost $\Gamma V+O(t)$ has $\delta=\sqrt t\,x_t$ with $x_t$ bounded, since the pair cost is nonnegative. Pass to a subsequence with $x_t\to x$. For $X\in E_t$ with $X=g+\operatorname{diag}(t^{3/4},t^{1/4})b$, the projection of $X-g$, divided by $t^{3/4}$, is $b_1+x_tb_2$, and the corresponding mark threshold is $t^{1/4}(v_{t,1}+\delta v_{t,2})\to0$. In this scaling the projected support is uniformly bounded and the shifts may be restricted to a fixed compact interval since larger absolute shifts give the saturated cost $V$. The cap areas on $B$ converge uniformly in that interval to the ones with the limiting normal and threshold. Otherwise a sequence of shifts witnessing failure has a convergent subsequence, and dominated convergence outside the two limiting area-null lines gives a contradiction. Therefore $P_t$ converges to $P_B((1,x))$, where $P_B(u)$ is the minimum of the two cap areas in $B$ with normal $u$ at thresholds $\sigma$ and $-\sigma$ over real $\sigma$. In this ray the smallest possible first-order score is
$$
-\kappa v_1+\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\{Vx^2/9+P_B((1,x))\}.
$$
Every fixed $x$ is attainable as a trial normal with $\delta=\sqrt t\,x$.

Since $B$ is a nondegenerate triangle of centroid zero, 6a7d56e450b3126f gives $P_B(u)\ge2\Gamma V$ for each $u\ne0$ and every opposite shift. The trial $x=\eta$ gives $2\Gamma V+V\eta^2/9$ for the expression being minimized. Thus any minimizer lies in $[-\eta,\eta]$. On this interval the determinant-one shear pulls $(1,x)$ back to $(1,q)$ on $T-g$, with $q=x-\eta\in[-1/5,0]$. After normalizing the three vertex heights $q,0,1$ to $0,a,1$, we have $a=-q/(1-q)\in[0,1/6]$ and centroid height $m=(1+a)/3$. For $a>0$ the fixed-normal analysis in the proof of d6ce3858d2712450 shows that any positive minimizing shift has saturated cost $V$ or lies on the proper straddling branch. The latter branch is strictly concave when $a<1/2$ and cannot have an interior minimum. The zero-shift cost is $2V(1-m)^2/(1-a)=2V(\Gamma+q^2/[9(1-q)])<V$, so the minimum is at zero. For $a=0$ the upper quadratic tail holds all the way down to the repeated lower vertex height. The two shifted proper caps then give a convex quadratic minimized at zero, and shifts beyond the lower support already cost at least $V$. Thus the expression is $2\Gamma V+(V/9)H(x)$ with $H(x)=x^2+2(x-\eta)^2/(1-x+\eta)$. We have
$$
H'(x)=2[x+(1-x+\eta)^{-2}-1],\qquad
H''(x)=2+4(1-x+\eta)^{-3}>0.
$$
The derivative is negative at zero and positive at $\eta$. Its unique zero gives the stated equation for $x_*$. Clearing denominators gives the cubic, whose signs at $6553/100000$ and $3277/50000$ are respectively negative and positive by substitution. The minimum excess is $\Delta>0$ since both squared terms could vanish simultaneously only if $\eta=0$.

In the other two ray neighborhoods, the $Y$ coefficient $u_2$ stays bounded away from zero and tends to the sign of the designated ray times a positive constant. The $E_t$ projection divided by $t^{1/4}$ has normal $(\sqrt t\,u_1,u_2)$ on $B$, and the mark threshold there is $O(t^{3/4})$. The same compact-shift argument gives limiting paired costs $P_B((0,1))$ for $l_2$ and $P_B((0,-1))$ for $l_0$, both $2\Gamma V$. Indeed the shear leaves $Y$ unchanged, so the positive vertical direction attains the bound at zero shift by the single-vertex cap formula. The negative vertical direction has centered projection $t-2/3$ with density $2t$ on $[0,1]$, giving the same minimum at shift $1/3$ by the planar equality calculation at the end of 37a5fc541beb1708 and the common lower bound 6a7d56e450b3126f. Positive scaling of the limiting normal only rescales the shifts. The own $T$ cap is smooth jointly in normal and mark in each canonical neighborhood. In fact, if $a_j=u\cdot(v_j-y)$ with simplex vertices $v_j$ and the cap isolates vertex $i$, its fraction is $a_i^2/\prod_{j\ne i}(a_i-a_j)$. At the canonical normal this cap equals $V(1-\lambda_i(y))^2$, with mark derivative $-\kappa l_i$ at $g$. Thus the mark change along a sequence of normals tending to the canonical one is $-t\kappa l_i(v)+o(t)$, and the own excess at $g$ is nonnegative. The exact canonical trial attains the lower first-order score for each of these two rays.

These lower bounds hold along subsequences of all minimizing normals, and the three stated trials provide the matching upper bounds. This proves the local expansion for every $v_t\to v$. At $v=(\Delta,-\Delta/2)$ the three first-order scores coincide. If a near-minimizing cap has normal approaching $l_1$, its own area bounds its scaled tilt as above. Every cluster point of that tilt must minimize the displayed expression, since its actual pair cost is at least the minimized pair cost. The unique minimizer is $x_*$, proving the tilt conclusion.

Finally, $\sum_i l_i(v)=0$ and the map $v\mapsto(l_0(v),l_1(v),l_2(v))$ has image the zero-sum plane. Hence the maximum of the minimum of the three first-order scores is their mean $\overline J=2\Gamma V+\Delta/3$, attained uniquely when all are equal, at $v=(\Delta,-\Delta/2)$. This mark displacement gives an admissible trial for small $t$. The $O(t)$ localization from e1209ac9a9de7caa applies to every local maximizing selection, so the local expansion along each convergent subsequence of rescaled displacements gives the maximum coefficient $\overline J$ and the asserted displacement for every selection. Adding the owned mass $tV$ gives the seven-fiber raw coefficient at base $(0,0)$. The other core maxima are at most $\Gamma V+tV$, and the added-base depths are at most $tV$, by the same accepted fact. Since $\overline J>0$, base $(0,0)$ wins strictly. Dividing by $4V+3tV$ gives the normalized formula. At $v=0$ the minimum of the scores is $2\Gamma V$, giving raw coefficient $V+2\Gamma V=17/18$ at the prescribed centroid there, while the bounds at the other cores give smaller coefficients.

statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ in $\mathbb R^2$ have area $V=1/2$ and centroid $g=(1/3,1/3)$. Write $\Gamma=4/9$, $\kappa=2/3$, $\eta=1/10$, $M_\eta(v_1,v_2)=(v_1-\eta v_2,v_2)$, $B=M_\eta(T-g)$, and
$$
E_t=g+\operatorname{diag}(t^{3/4},t^{1/4})B.
$$
Place $T$ at each of the four binary integer bases, and $E_t$ at $(-1,0),(-1,1),(1,-1)$, and take their actual convex hull. Let $A_{6,t}(y)$ be raw closed-halfspace mixed depth at $((0,0),y)$ in the hull after omitting the fiber at $(-1,0)$. Define $l_1(v)=v_1$, $l_2(v)=v_2$, and $l_0(v)=-v_1-v_2$. Let $x_*$ be the unique root in $(0,\eta)$ of $(1-x)(1-x+\eta)^2=1$, or equivalently $100x^3-320x^2+341x-21=0$. It satisfies $6553/100000<x_*<3277/50000$. Put
$$
\Delta=\frac V9\left(x_*^2+\frac{2(x_*-\eta)^2}{1-x_*+\eta}\right)>0,
\qquad J_0=J_2=2\Gamma V,\qquad J_1=2\Gamma V+\Delta.
$$
For every convergent bounded sequence $v_t\to v$,
$$
A_{6,t}(g+tv_t)=\Gamma V+t\min_{0\le i\le2}\{J_i-\kappa l_i(v)\}+o(t).
$$
At marks with $y=g+t(\Delta,-\Delta/2)+o(t)$, every six-fiber through-mark cap sequence within $o(t)$ of the minimum and with continuous normals approaching the canonical $l_1$ direction has $\delta_t/\sqrt t\to x_*$ under positive normalization of those normals to $(1,\delta_t)$.

For all sufficiently small $t>0$, the global maximum in the seven-fiber source is attained, every maximizing point has integer base $(0,0)$, and its continuous mark is $y_t=g+t(\Delta,-\Delta/2)+o(t)$. With total mixed mass $M_t=4V+3tV$, the raw and normalized maxima are
$$
D_t=\frac29+t\left(\frac{17}{18}+\frac\Delta3\right)+o(t),
\qquad
D_t/M_t=\frac19+t\left(\frac7{18}+\frac\Delta6\right)+o(t).
$$
At the core centroid with base $(0,0)$ the raw first-order coefficient is $17/18$, and the other three core centroids have smaller coefficients.
title: Quadratic normal-motion cost in an anisotropic seven-fiber depth response
